A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 25-page Hilbert-Geo paper, including Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–25 are identical; page 1 has only an availability-statement revision and updated arXiv stamp. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original parsing and reasoning experiments, human comparisons, and error analyses in Section 6 and Appendices C and E, including results on SolidFGeo2k, MathVerse-Solid, and PlaneFGeo3k.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendices C and E.

M1.justification: The Parse2Reason pipeline, multimodal formalization parser, predicate and theorem libraries, and SGRE search procedure are unchanged, including Algorithm 1 and the appendix specifications.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SolidFGeo2k, PlaneFGeo3k, and MathVerse-Solid with the same solid and plane geometry tasks and fine-grained subject coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 1–2 and 9–11 retain identical comparator membership, including the MLLM baselines, human comparisons, and ground-truth-CDL controls.

E3.justification: The evaluation settings are unchanged, including 15/25/35/45-example configurations, the 50-student human comparison, accuracy and parsing metrics, and timeout-testing procedures.

E4.justification: Section 6.3 and the appendices retain the same example-count analyses, component-wise parsing evaluations, error analyses, and timeout-relaxation experiment. No analysis or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 6.1 retains the same statement of five evaluation rounds. Repeated-run information and statistical reporting are unchanged; no uncertainty estimates or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative findings are unchanged. Hilbert-Geo retains 77.3% accuracy on SolidFGeo2k (Table 1), 84.1% on MathVerse-Solid (Table 9), and 80.2% on PlaneFGeo3k (Table 11).

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the same solid-composition definition and Theorems A.1–A.3 with their proofs. The mathematical definitions and evaluation algorithms in Appendix C are also identical.

C1.justification: The scientific claims about unified solid-geometry formalization, the parser and reasoning engine, the two curated datasets, and performance and generality remain unchanged in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: The explanations of parsing quality, hallucinations, combinatorial-explosion failures, and defective problem conditions are unchanged, as are the applicability and mechanism discussions.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from saying code and datasets 'will be publicly available' to stating they 'are released' and supplies the PremiLab-Math/Hilbert-Geo repository link. This adds concrete access information; implementation details and appendix prompts remain unchanged. Repository availability and contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, references, and positioning relative to FormalGeo and other geometry-solving approaches are identical. The new project link does not introduce a cited research work.

P1.justification: Only the abstract's final availability sentence and the arXiv version/date stamp change. The remaining wording, headings, terminology, and document organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. The first-page sentence replacement preserves the layout; the updated marginal arXiv stamp does not constitute a layout revision.

improvement.justification: v3 replaces a future-release promise with a stated release and a concrete code/data repository link, modestly improving reproducibility documentation and resource discoverability. The scientific content and supporting evidence remain identical. This benefit concerns the documented access route; the PDFs alone do not establish repository completeness or usability.
